papers.title: MinNav: Minimalist Navigation Using Optical Flow For Active Tiny Aerial Robots
papers.summary: Navigation using a monocular camera is pivotal for autonomous operation on tiny aerial robots due to their perfect balance of versatility, cost and accuracy. In this paper, we introduce MinNav, a navigation stack based on optical flow and its uncertainty to fly through a scene with static and dynamic obstacles and unknown-shaped gaps without any prior knowledge of the scene components and/or their locations/ordering. We further improve success rate by using the activeness of the robot to move around in an exploratory way to find obstacles and navigate. We successfully evaluate and demonstrate the proposed approach in many real-world experiments in various environments with static and dynamic obstacles and unknown-shaped gaps with an overall success rate of 70%. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first solution to tackle all the aforementioned navigation cases without prior knowledge using a monocular camera. Our approach is on par in performance with depth based methods with factors of magnitude less computation required and can readily run onboard tiny aerial robots. The accompanying video, supplementary material, code and dataset can be found at https://pear.wpi.edu/research/minnav.html

papers.title: IntentNav: Learning Spatial-Visual Object Navigation from Human Demonstrations
papers.summary: Object navigation requires a robot to search for an unobserved target in an unknown environment by deciding where to explore next under partial observability. Effective search resembles human-like exploration: selectively probing visually promising frontiers while relying on spatial memory to avoid redundant revisits. We propose IntentNav, a spatial-visual imitation framework that learns human-like ObjectNav policies from human demonstrations. To infer high-level search intent from low-level human actions, we introduce Frontier-based Human-Intent Labeling, which looks ahead in human demonstrations and labels the frontier that best explains the demonstrator's future search direction. We construct a spatial-visual candidate space, where BEV memory tracks explored regions, unexplored frontiers, and trajectory history, while egocentric visual memory provides semantic cues for each candidate. A VLM policy is trained to select among these grounded candidates, using Intent-Aligned Objective to encourage consistent and human-like exploration. IntentNav achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MP3D, HM3D-v1 and HM3D-v2 ObjectNav benchmarks. The proposed candidate-level navigation interface transfers zero-shot to wheeled, quadruped, and humanoid robots without further VLM fine-tuning. \href{https://anonymous.4open.science/w/IntentNav/}{Project page}.

openclaw.abstract_zh: 目标导航要求机器人在未知环境和部分可观测条件下搜索未观测目标，并决定下一步探索哪里。有效搜索类似人类探索：选择视觉上有希望的前沿，同时依靠空间记忆避免重复访问。论文提出 IntentNav，一种从人类示范学习人类式 ObjectNav 策略的空间-视觉模仿框架。为从低层人类动作中推断高层搜索意图，论文提出基于前沿的人类意图标注方法，通过向前查看人类示范，标注最能解释示范者未来搜索方向的前沿。论文构建空间-视觉候选空间，其中 BEV 记忆记录已探索区域、未探索前沿和轨迹历史，自我中心视觉记忆为每个候选提供语义线索。训练 VLM 策略在这些具身候选中选择，并使用意图对齐目标鼓励一致且类人的探索。IntentNav 在 MP3D、HM3D-v1 和 HM3D-v2 ObjectNav 基准上达到最先进性能，候选级导航接口可零样本迁移到轮式、四足和人形机器人，无需进一步 VLM 微调。

papers.title: Affordance-Based Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Quadruped Pedipulation
papers.summary: The object manipulation capabilities of quadruped robots is an open research challenge. While previous studies have focused on low-level policy learning, task execution still relies on expert-designed high-level trajectories. Autonomous selection of both an affordable interaction point on the target object and an affordable robot base pose removes the need for pre-designed trajectories. This study proposes a three-level hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework that utilizes pose affordances to guide the navigation policy, while the navigation policy drives the locomotion policy. In addition, the pedipulation policy is guided by interaction-point affordances, enabling object-centric pose alignment of the quadruped robot and effective end-effector manipulation planning. We train the proposed framework in the IsaacSim ecosystem and evaluate it in both simulation and real-world settings. We investigate the effectiveness of pose affordance across multiple scenarios in simulation while various object interaction tasks are validated on real-world setting forming an object-interaction dataset. The results show that the proposed framework can autonomously identify candidate poses based on their affordance and successfully execute object manipulation tasks in the real world without human guidance.

openclaw.title_zh: 基于可供性的四足机器人层级强化学习足部操作
openclaw.solved_problem_zh: 这篇论文解决了四足机器人在物体交互任务中依赖人工设计高层轨迹、难以自主选择交互点和机器人基座位姿的问题。
openclaw.tldr_zh: 论文用三层层级强化学习，让四足机器人根据可供性自主导航到合适位姿并完成物体操作。
openclaw.relevance_zh: 与具身智能导航相关，重点在导航策略、位姿选择、空间对齐和真实机器人执行；虽然不是VLN、ObjectNav或PointNav，但涉及机器人面向物体交互的导航与规划策略。
openclaw.problem_zh: 四足机器人具备物体操作能力仍是开放挑战；已有方法多关注低层策略学习，而任务执行仍依赖专家设计的高层轨迹，限制了自主性。
openclaw.method_zh: 提出三层层级强化学习框架：使用位姿可供性指导导航策略，导航策略驱动运动策略；同时用交互点可供性指导足部操作策略，实现面向物体的位姿对齐和末端执行器操作规划。
openclaw.contribution_zh: 核心贡献是将位姿可供性和交互点可供性引入四足机器人层级强化学习，使机器人能够自主选择候选基座位姿与交互点，并在仿真和真实场景中执行物体操作任务。
key_contributions_zh: 提出基于可供性的三层层级强化学习框架，连接导航策略、运动策略和足部操作策略
利用位姿可供性指导机器人基座导航与物体中心位姿对齐
在IsaacSim中训练，并在仿真和真实世界中评估物体交互任务
openclaw.experiments_zh: 摘要说明在IsaacSim生态中训练，在仿真和真实世界中评估；仿真中考察多场景下位姿可供性的有效性，真实环境中验证多种物体交互任务并形成物体交互数据集。
openclaw.limitations_zh: 摘要未说明，需要看正文核验。
openclaw.read_suggestion_zh: 建议关注层级策略如何把可供性用于导航位姿选择，以及真实机器人验证是否能为ObjectNav式目标交互导航提供参考。
openclaw.abstract_zh: 四足机器人的物体操作能力仍是开放研究挑战。以往研究多关注低层策略学习，但任务执行仍依赖专家设计的高层轨迹。自主选择目标物体上可交互的交互点和机器人基座可行位姿，可以避免预设计轨迹。本文提出三层层级强化学习框架，利用位姿可供性指导导航策略，并由导航策略驱动运动策略。同时，足部操作策略由交互点可供性指导，使四足机器人能够进行面向物体的位姿对齐和有效的末端执行器操作规划。该框架在IsaacSim中训练，并在仿真和真实世界中评估。研究在仿真多场景中考察位姿可供性的有效性，并在真实环境中验证多种物体交互任务，形成物体交互数据集。结果表明，该框架能够基于可供性自主识别候选位姿，并在无人指导下于真实世界成功执行物体操作任务。
